cls: Ergot alkaloid mixture / cognitive and mood enhancer in age-related mental decline (ergoloid mesylates; dihydroergotoxine)
pharm: A mixture of the methanesulfonate (mesylate) salts of four dihydrogenated ergot alkaloids (dihydroergocornine, dihydroergocristine, and the alpha and beta isomers of dihydroergocryptine) in fixed proportions; it has weak alpha-adrenergic blocking and partial dopaminergic/serotonergic activity and is proposed to act on neuronal metabolism and neurotransmission rather than primarily as a cerebral vasodilator.
quick: 1 mg orally three times daily; some regimens use 4.5 mg/day up to about 12 mg/day
May be taken without regard to meals; sublingual tablets are dissolved under the tongue
Not indicated in women of childbearing potential; ergot derivative - avoid in pregnancy
Avoid; ergot alkaloids may suppress lactation and excretion into milk is not established
No specific dosage adjustment established in the labeling
Use with caution; extensively metabolized by the liver
Avoid or limit alcohol; both can affect mental status in older adults
Reassess diagnosis and response periodically; exclude reversible/underlying causes; heart rate
summary: Codergocrine mesylate (ergoloid mesylates; formerly dihydroergotoxine, brand Hydergine) is an FDA-approved fixed mixture of dihydrogenated ergot alkaloids indicated for older adults (generally over 60) with signs and symptoms of an idiopathic decline in mental capacity. The FDA labeling is deliberately cautious about effectiveness: the drug may provide symptomatic relief of mood and cognitive complaints, but there is no specific underlying disease entity that has been identified, the measurable improvement is modest, and the effectiveness in any specific patient is not established. Treatable causes of mental decline (such as depression, delirium, metabolic or endocrine disturbance, dementia of known cause, or normal-pressure hydrocephalus) must be excluded before and during treatment. The usual oral dose is 1 mg three times daily, with some regimens using 4.5 to 12 mg per day; a clinical response, if it occurs, may take several weeks to develop. It is contraindicated in acute or chronic psychosis regardless of cause and in patients hypersensitive to the drug.
indications: Treatment of signs and symptoms of an idiopathic decline in mental capacity in older patients (generally over 60 years) who show some cognitive and/or mood impairment thought to be age-related, where a specific underlying treatable disease has been excluded
Used to provide modest symptomatic relief of mood and cognitive complaints; effectiveness in any individual patient is not established and there is no identified specific underlying disease entity

dosage.c: Idiopathic decline in mental capacity (older adults)
dosage.n: Usual labeled dose; benefit, if present, may take several weeks and should be reassessed periodically

dosage.d: Approximately 4.5 mg per day, with some regimens up to about 12 mg per day in divided doses
dosage.n: Higher total daily doses have been used in clinical practice; titrate to response and tolerability

dosage.d: 1 mg three times daily (equivalent to the oral tablet dose)
dosage.n: Allow sublingual tablets to dissolve completely under the tongue; oral liquid may be used as an alternative

dosage.d: Continue for an adequate trial (several weeks to months) before judging response
dosage.n: Discontinue if no meaningful symptomatic improvement and re-evaluate the underlying cause

admin: Confirm the diagnosis of idiopathic age-related decline by first excluding reversible and specific treatable causes (depression, delirium, metabolic/endocrine disorders, drug effects, dementia of identifiable cause)
Give the oral tablet without regard to meals; the usual schedule is three times daily
For sublingual tablets, place under the tongue and allow to dissolve completely - do not chew or swallow whole
Allow an adequate treatment trial of several weeks, as any benefit develops gradually
Reassess the diagnosis and the need for continued therapy periodically; stop if no benefit
moa: Codergocrine (ergoloid) mesylates are a mixture of the mesylate salts of dihydrogenated ergot peptide alkaloids (dihydroergocornine, dihydroergocristine, dihydroergocryptine). The precise mechanism by which the drug produces mental effects has not been established, and the effects were originally and incorrectly attributed to cerebral vasodilation. Current understanding is that the dihydrogenated ergot alkaloids act centrally on neuronal metabolism and on neurotransmitter systems - they possess weak alpha-adrenergic blocking activity and interact with dopaminergic and serotonergic receptors, and may influence synaptic transmission and neuronal metabolic activity. The drug is not a specific treatment for any defined pathologic entity, and its clinical benefit in age-related mental decline, where present, is modest and of uncertain mechanism.

absolute: Acute or chronic psychosis, regardless of etiology
Known hypersensitivity to codergocrine (ergoloid) mesylates or any ergot alkaloid or component of the formulation
relative: Bradycardia or significant cardiac disease (the drug can lower heart rate)
monitor: Mental status and any worsening confusion or emergence of psychotic features
Periodic reassessment of the diagnosis to exclude an evolving treatable cause
Overall clinical response to justify continued therapy

preg: Codergocrine mesylate is indicated for older adults and is not intended for use in women of childbearing potential. As an ergot alkaloid derivative, it should be avoided in pregnancy; adequate data on use in human pregnancy are lacking and ergot compounds have potential effects on uterine and vascular tone.
lact: Use during breastfeeding should be avoided. Ergot alkaloids can suppress lactation, and excretion of codergocrine into human milk has not been adequately characterized. Given the indication is in older adults, lactation is rarely relevant, but the drug should not be used in nursing mothers.
renal: The labeling does not specify a particular dosage adjustment for renal impairment, as the drug is eliminated predominantly by hepatic metabolism. Use general caution in significant renal impairment and titrate to response and tolerability.
hepatic: Codergocrine is extensively metabolized by the liver and undergoes substantial first-pass metabolism, so plasma concentrations may be increased in hepatic impairment. Use with caution in patients with liver disease and consider lower doses.

major: Other ergot alkaloids and ergotamine-type agents - additive vasoconstrictive/ergot effects; avoid combination
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors) - may raise ergoloid exposure and toxicity
moderate: Antihypertensive and other blood-pressure-lowering agents - additive hypotension
Drugs that lower heart rate (e.g., beta-blockers) - additive bradycardia
Dopaminergic and serotonergic agents - possible additive central effects
minor: Other centrally acting drugs in older adults may compound effects on mental status
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; no clinically significant food interaction is established.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol should be avoided or limited; it can worsen cognition and mood in older adults and may add to any sedative or vasomotor effects.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference is established; monitor heart rate and blood pressure clinically.

serious: Orthostatic hypotension with dizziness or falls
Worsening of psychotic symptoms (use is contraindicated in psychosis)
emergency: Signs of ergotism with overdose (peripheral vasospasm, ischemia)

monitoring: Heart rate (the drug can produce bradycardia) and blood pressure
Mental status and any emergence or worsening of confusion or psychotic features
Periodic reassessment of the diagnosis to exclude an evolving or previously missed treatable cause of mental decline
Objective and subjective response to therapy to justify continuation
Tolerability, including gastrointestinal upset and orthostatic symptoms
counsel: This medicine may give modest help with mood and thinking symptoms, but it does not cure the underlying condition and may not work for everyone
Take it exactly as prescribed, usually one tablet three times a day
If you are given tablets that dissolve under the tongue, let them dissolve completely - do not chew or swallow them whole
Any benefit develops slowly over weeks, so keep taking it as directed and do not expect an immediate change
Tell your doctor if your heart feels slow, if you feel dizzy or faint when standing, or if confusion or unusual thoughts get worse
Your doctor will check from time to time whether the medicine is still helping and will look for other treatable causes of memory or mood changes
pk: Gradual; symptomatic benefit, if any, develops over several weeks
Plasma Tmax within about 1-2 hours after oral/sublingual dosing
Variable; terminal elimination of the alkaloid components on the order of several hours (reported up to ~13 hours)
Dosed multiple times daily (typically three times) to sustain effect
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light; keep tightly closed
pearls: Codergocrine mesylate IS FDA-approved as ergoloid mesylates (brand Hydergine); it is not an unapproved supplement
The FDA labeling is intentionally cautious - effectiveness is not definitively established and any measurable improvement is modest
Exclude reversible and specific treatable causes of mental decline (depression, delirium, metabolic/endocrine disease, drug effects, identifiable dementia) before and during treatment
Contraindicated in acute or chronic psychosis regardless of cause and in hypersensitivity to ergot alkaloids
Usual dose is 1 mg three times daily; some regimens use 4.5 to 12 mg/day, with benefit emerging only after weeks
Watch for bradycardia and orthostatic hypotension, especially in frail older adults
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Overdose may cause exaggerated pharmacologic effects such as nausea, marked bradycardia, hypotension, flushing, and, with large amounts of an ergot alkaloid, features of ergotism (peripheral vasospasm and ischemia). Management is symptomatic and supportive, including monitoring of heart rate and blood pressure, supportive care for hypotension and bradycardia, and standard gastrointestinal decontamination measures where appropriate.
